questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements about linked list and array?
S1 : Random access is not allowed in implementation of linked list.
S2 : Insertion and deletion of elements in easy in linked list than array.
S3 : Array has better cache locality than linked list which make array preferable in terms of performance.
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
(d)
• Random access is not allowed in linked list but allowed in array.
• Insertion and deletion in array is difficult, since we need to shifts other elements, while insertion and deletion in linked list in easy (only few pointers need to be charged in worst case both take Ο(n) time).
• Since array are contiguous memory blocks, so large chunk of them will be loaded into the cache upon cache upon first access. Which make cache access faster for future elements of array i.e. gives better cache locality which is not possible in case of linked list.

questions.qtext: What is the time complexity of the following code?
questions.solution:
(a)
Time complexity of finding the maximum element in a binary tree: The function findMax recursively traverses the binary tree to find the maximum element. At each node, it compares the value of the current node with the maximum value obtained from its left and right subtrees. Since the function visits each node once, the time complexity is Ο(n), where n is the number of nodes in the binary tree.

questions.qtext: What does the following code snippet do?

options.text: Counts the number of leaf nodes in a binary search tree
Deletes all leaf nodes from a binary tree
Finds the diameter of a binary tree
Searches for a given value in a binary tree

questions.solution:
(a)
Counting leaf nodes in a binary tree: This code snippet counts the number of leaf nodes in a binary tree. It recursively traverses the tree and checks if a node is a leaf node (i.e., it has no left and right children). If a node is a leaf node, it returns 1; otherwise, it recursively counts the leaf nodes in its left and right subtrees and adds them. The final count represents the total number of leaf nodes in the binary tree.
